findings.quote: "more of an energy your chart already holds in excess" · "the energy your chart already has too much of" · "piling more onto a chart already full of it" · "though your chart is already crowded with it" · "adding pressure your chart already has in plenty"
findings.issue: `energyState` returns `heavy` for any friction energy whatever its volume (`s < 0 → 'heavy'`). In the 600-chart sample, 315 of 1,173 and 317 of 1,248 heavy energies are thin (≤10%). That is about one heavy line in four telling a reader they hold "too much" of an energy they barely have. Example: born 1996-05-19 16h, Overfueled Wood, Water = Mind at 1% → "Water brings Mind, the energy your chart already has too much of." Each unit is shared by every chart in the state, so the claim has to hold for thin charts too.
findings.fix: **Rule:** a heavy or core_over line names the *valence*, not the *amount*: "more than your chart can use", "more than your chart is built for", "an energy your chart does better with less of". Never "already holds / has / carries too much", "full of", "crowded with", "in plenty", "in excess". Examples: `mind · day.heavy.a` (golden) → "{el} brings Mind, more than your chart can use today. Your thoughts circle, and you get less done than you meant to." · `order · day.heavy.b` → "{el} brings Order, a weight your chart does better with less of. A deadline tightens or a rule bites, and you work twice as hard for the same result." · `action · month.heavy` → "{el} brings Action for a whole month, more reach than your chart is built for. Work spreads thin across too many fronts, and you feel stretched by the third week." The same rule applies to Life Chapters' year lines (O1).

findings.issue: The second sentence of almost every friction landing resolves the bond with the reader's ideal behaviour and a good outcome. That causes four problems. (1) It flatters, which BIZ_04 names as the fastest way to lose this audience. (2) It claims an outcome no twelve-day cycle can know. (3) It is advice dressed as fact, outside the favours rows where ruling D1 B allows advice. (4) It cancels its own bond, so a harm ("wears thin") ends with the warmth intact, and it pre-empts the favours row that offers the choice ("Fixing it quietly over raising it"). The grow lines do the same with guaranteed wins.
findings.fix: **Rule:** a landing's second sentence names what the event stirs in the reader (the felt pull, the old wish, the private conflict), never how it ends and never a comparison with others; the choice belongs to the favours row. A grow line names what becomes possible, not the result. Examples. harm.year: "A remark from an older relative lands wrong, though nobody meant it unkindly. You hear the old family verdict in it, and it stings more than the words do." clash.day: "A plan at home changes at short notice, with a partner or whoever you live with. You go along with it out loud and keep the disappointment to yourself." punish.month: "Friction at work returns, the same complaint from the same corner of the team. You feel the old tiredness of making the same case twice." order.grow.b: "Wood brings Order, adding to a discipline you already keep. A standard you set yourself gets tested today, and you are glad of the habits you built."

findings.pages: 30 of 34; all 13 friction-bond landings (clash, punish, harm): D052 D057 D060 D065 D069 D074 D077 D088 D089 D094 D100 D101 D113
findings.quote: "You settle it by evening, on your own terms." · "You adjust faster than the people around you." · "Someone checks your work today, and you pass the test." · "nothing you say comes out wrong" · "you choose well" · "end the day stronger than you began" · "you answer for it calmly" · "You catch the moment and put it right before bed."
findings.issue: The reader wins almost every closing sentence. On friction bonds this removes the cost the bond names (clash = shaken, punish = grinds, harm = wears thin). That fails BIZ_04's sugarcoat test ("the cost is missing or shrunk"), and it is the flattery this audience drops apps for. It also states outcomes the day cannot know ("you pass", "you settle it by evening"). Of 13 friction landings, 13 end in a win. Of the energy lines, 14 of 22 distinct units end on a guaranteed success
findings.fix: Rule: on clash, punish and harm, sentence two names the plain cost in the reader's own week and leaves the reader the choice, not the result. Example: "A plan at home changes at short notice, with a partner or the people you live with. You lose the evening you had set aside and choose what to keep from it." On grow and need energy lines, say what the energy makes easier, not that the reader succeeds. Keep at most one win close per page. Rebuild: the 13 friction landings (×4 gates), the grow/need/even energy b-sentences, and the yuede and tiande stars

findings.quote: "Fire brings Action, the energy your chart lacks most." (D088) · "Earth brings Order, the energy your chart is shortest of." (D091) · "Earth brings Order, the energy you need most." (D094), all for the same reader (癸, 1995-12-08)
findings.issue: The need state is shared by every needed function, but the unit claims a rank. One reader sees three different energies called "most" or "shortest" on three days. On this chart Fire is the true shortfall, so the Earth lines are false. A unit cannot know a rank it is not keyed on
findings.fix: Rule: no superlative in a need unit unless the engine passes the rank. Rewrite the six openers as "the energy your chart runs short on", "the outlet your chart is short of", "the support you run short on" and similar, then vary the rest of the line. Example: "Earth brings Order, an energy your chart runs short on. A rule or a deadline lands on you today, and you find it steadies you."

findings.issue: (a) The brief locks the relation words as "feeds · shapes", but three of the five ground units use other verbs: "holds down", "pushes back against", "draws … off". (b) The tails are the same whether the energy is grown or released. "You put both to work" calls a released energy useful (D052, D116-type pages), against A1's rule that a released energy is never welcome. findings.fix: Rebuild the five ground units on the locked verbs, with the tail saying what the ground does to the day's energy, not to the reader's mood. presses: "Under it runs Water, which the Earth shapes, so the day's push lands on solid ground." resists: "Under it runs Water, which shapes the Fire, so the day's energy meets a check from below." drains: "Under it runs Wood, which the Water feeds, so the day's energy spends itself as it goes." feeds: "Under it runs Metal, which feeds the Water, so the day's energy keeps its strength." matches: "Under it runs more Wood, so the day's energy comes at full strength." The reader stays in the next unit's last sentence. If a grow/release-aware tail is wanted, that is an engine change

findings.quote: "the energy your chart already has too much of" (M036, M063); "more strain on a chart already full of it" (M018, M021); "though you already pour out plenty"; "though your chart is already crowded with it"
findings.issue: The engine sets `heavy` for **every** released energy whatever its share (`engine/almanac/index.js:153`: `if (s < 0) return 'heavy'`), yet all four lines claim volume. Chart 乙亥 庚辰 己卯 癸酉 has no Fire in a stem, branch or hidden stem, and is told it has too much Fire. The 甲 chart holds Metal only as hidden 辛 and is told it is "full of" Metal. Classically (子平真诠, 论用神) the energy is released because of the Day Master's strength: an Underfueled core cannot carry the drain of Expression, Action and Order, and an Overfueled core does not need Mind. Its share is not the reason. mind.heavy also ends in praise ("you hold your ground well") for an energy the reader releases.
findings.fix: Rule: a `heavy` line names why the reader releases the energy (the strength of the core), never its volume, unless the engine splits `heavy` by share (≥20%). Each of these keys reaches only one condition, so the rewrites can say so: **expression.heavy** "{El} brings Expression for a whole month, more output than your chart can fund. You start many things and show them early, and your strength runs low by the last week." **action.heavy** "{El} brings Action for a whole month, more than your strength can carry. Tasks spread thin across too many fronts, and you feel stretched by the third week." **order.heavy** "{El} brings Order for a whole month, more pressure than your chart can carry. Rules and demands fill your weeks, and you get through them by keeping your head down." **mind.heavy** "{El} brings Mind for a whole month, more support than your strong chart needs. You think longer and move slower, and you hold on where you should let go." Check `ENERGY … day.heavy` for the same claim.

findings.quote: "You and the people closest to you come out of it on firmer footing"; "by the month's end it has less hold on you"; "You reach out first, and the distance closes"; "trust returns by the month's end"; "the arguments shrink as the weeks pass"; "You end the month with fewer duties and a firmer hold"
findings.issue: Every clash, punish and harm resolves in the reader's favour inside the month. That predicts a result the cycle cannot know (the brief: no fate). It turns each friction into a reassurance, the sugarcoat BIZ_04 warns this audience punishes. Classically 冲 shakes, 刑 grinds and 害 wears (三命通会, 论刑冲破害), and none of these carries a resolution. The reader also never meets the friction itself, because the closing promise comes too fast.
findings.fix: Rule: a landing's second sentence names what the reader meets or feels during the month, not how it ends. Ban "by the month's end", "closes", "returns", "shrink", "firmer footing". Examples: **clash.day** "Your home life is shaken up this month, in the furniture, the plans or the shape of a shared week. You feel the ground move under habits you thought were settled." **harm.year** "A coolness creeps into the family you grew up in this month, from a word taken badly or a call left unreturned. You notice the silence before anyone names it." **punish.year** "A family grievance from years back grinds on through this month, raised at each visit or call. You hear the old lines again and know them by heart." Check the Day and Year landings for the same pattern.

findings.pages: M046, M110 (2 of 36; every chart where the month repeats one gate's branch and half-frames another)
findings.quote: M046: "The month's Water joins the Water in your Year Gate" (亥 month, 亥 year); M110: "The month's Water joins the Water in your Month Gate" (亥 month, 亥 month gate)
findings.issue: The real bond is the 亥卯 half-frame with the **Day Gate's** 卯. `branchBonds` puts every node whose branch belongs to the frame into `gates`, so a gate that holds the same 亥 as the month counts as a frame partner, and the almanac lands on it. A branch cannot frame itself (三命通会, 论三合: three different branches, or two with the 旺 centre). So the reader gets "your wider family pulls together" (Year Gate) or "Work builds speed" (Month Gate) when the bond sits in home and partner.
findings.fix: Code rule: in a frame, leave out any gate whose branch equals the passing branch, and land on a gate holding a different member (here the Day Gate's 卯, giving `land.month.frame.day`). Add a golden case: 1995-04-18 18:00 × 2026-11; 1992-12-05 22:00 × 2026-11.

findings.pages: presses: M002 M013 M027 M036 M046 M059 M076 M086 M095 M102 M106 M110; drains, feeds, matches: the other 24
findings.quote: "Under it runs Metal, which the Fire holds down, and you put both to work."
findings.issue: "holds down" replaces the locked relation word "shapes". "you put both to work" means nothing a reader can check, and it adds a "work" to pages already stacking it (7 pages at "work" ×3–5). All four ground units close on ", and you …", which puts the joint "and you" twice or more on 30 of 36 pages. The relations themselves are all right: 干克支 spends the stem's force (盖头), 干生支 leaks it, 支生干 roots it.
findings.fix: **presses** "Under it runs {G}, which the {El} shapes, so part of its push is spent before it reaches you." **drains** "Under it runs {G}, which the {El} feeds, so the push reaches you softer week by week." **feeds** "Under it runs {G}, which feeds the {El}, so it stays with you from the first week to the last." **matches** "Under it runs more {El}, so it reaches you at full strength."

findings.quote: "Nothing in the day reaches your gates, and life runs on its usual track. You have the time and the calm to do things at your own pace."
findings.issue: On a Month page it says "the day". On M013 it promises "time and the calm" under an energy line that says "you feel stretched by the third week". findings.pages: Y099, Y103 (2 of 14 Year pages; same code serves Day and Month)
findings.quote: "The year's Fire joins the Fire in your Year Gate, the seat of your first home."
findings.issue: For 半合/三合, `engine/almanac/index.js:182` takes `b.gates.find(g => g !== 'now')`, which is the first natal gate holding *any* member of the set. When the natal chart already holds the passing branch (午), it picks that gate. In Y099 (庚午 丙戌 …) the partner is 戌 in the Month Gate. In Y103 (庚午 丁亥 壬寅 …) the partner is 寅 in the Day Gate. "Fire joins the Fire" is not a frame. 午 meeting 午 is 自刑 (三命通会 论三刑: 辰午酉亥自刑), which is the house's *repeat*. Result: the landing, the headline ("your family gathers round") and the domain weight all go to the wrong gate
findings.fix: Rule: a frame lands on the gate whose branch is the **partner**, meaning it is in the 三合 set and is *different* from the passing branch. With several partners, pick the higher-weighted gate. A natal gate holding the same branch as the passing one is read only as repeat/自刑, never as frame. Re-run the Year (and Day/Month) covers after the fix

You lose time to questions you thought were closed, and you close them properly this time." (31 words)
